name: Laughing Hyenas
label: Touch and Go
lede: John Brannon left hardcore behind, Larissa Strickland taught herself guitar in an Ann Arbor basement, and Butch Vig miked their PA so loud he worried about his fillings. Ten years, three albums, and a sound Brannon says nobody can recreate.

eras.title: Out of the Cass Corridor
eras.text: Brannon had fronted Negative Approach; his girlfriend Larissa Stolarchuk sang in the Detroit post-punk band L-Seven. Both bands were finished, their gear kept getting stolen, and a show by The Birthday Party had convinced them rock needed starting over. So they drove to Ann Arbor with a drummer and no place to stay.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: Brannon, Stolarchuk and a drummer live out of a van in Ann Arbor
years.p: With drummer Mike Danner, the couple leave Detroit's Cass Corridor and sleep in Brannon's van for a couple of weeks. Bassist Kevin Monroe moves into the house they eventually rent.
years.xp:
Brannon told Metro Times they crashed on the couches at the Michigan Union ballroom because it had cable and a bathroom, and raided frat-house kitchens by claiming they "knew John," since every frat house had a John.

Stolarchuk started on bass, then moved to guitar, an instrument she had never played. Monroe agreed to take bass and set out to write riffs so bass-heavy the band couldn't replace him. Later both took the surname Strickland.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: First show: warming up for Destroy All Monsters
years.p: The Hyenas debut at Joe's Star Lounge in Ann Arbor opening for Destroy All Monsters, with ex-[[MC5|08b736bb-1c82-40b4-8b0b-49e2182a067a]] bassist Mike Davis in the headliners. Negative Approach's crowd doesn't follow Brannon over.
years.xp:
Brannon wanted a band untouched by the whole rock thing; the reference points were Alice Cooper, the Birthday Party and The Gun Club. Danner remembered rehearsing like crazy and, for what felt like years, having about six songs.

The punk audience, Brannon said, was still holding on to the super-hardcore thing. The Hyenas did not go over well.

years.cap: Kimball, Strickland, Monroe and Brannon in a Touch and Go promo photo
years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: A torn tab at Schoolkids Records brings in Jim Kimball
years.p: Danner leaves after fights over touring, recording and sharing a house. The only person to answer the band's "Wanted, punk blues drummer" ad is [[Jim Kimball|93ed63b4-5dc3-4f4d-9a74-b891e0354b76]], who has never met any of them.
years.xp:
Kimball came from a jazzier, light-tapping style. Brannon's instruction was simple: "Jim, don't tap, pound." Kimball switched to thicker sticks with no tips. Danner went on to drum in Big Chief.

That same year the band cut a demo at an east-side Detroit studio. Touch and Go owner Corey Rusk's verdict, as Brannon remembers it: you guys aren't quite ready.

eras.title: Five days at Smart Studios, three times
eras.text: Rusk kept telling Butch Vig the Hyenas were ferocious, and Vig recorded their first three records in Madison on Touch and Go budgets of about a week each. They toured with Sonic Youth, met Nirvana, and became one of the bands Vig points to when people ask how he ended up making Nevermind.

years.big: "The fillings in your teeth would fall out."
q: It was like the fillings in your teeth would fall out.
years.src: Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Vig puts the band's own PA in the studio
years.p: Brannon wanted his vocals cut through a live PA, the way he'd read [[The Stooges|794c6bf2-3241-416f-9b8f-24e2d84a1c4b]] did Fun House. Vig miked the PA, and Strickland set her Fender Twin to 10.
years.xp:
Vig had never done it that way before, Brannon says, and went with it. Vig's recollection is that each record took about five days, at roughly $500 a day for the studio, and he guesses each cost about three grand.

He also remembers almost never having to edit. Two or three takes, tops: the rhythm section was that tight.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas · Detroit Metro Times · Trouser Press
years.h: Touch and Go puts out Come Down to the Merry Go Round
years.p: Six songs on a 12-inch, produced with Vig. Monroe and Stolarchuk are credited as Strickland for the first time.
years.xp: That November the band played much of it, plus songs for the next record, live on Ann Arbor's WCBN-FM. Locally they were opening for whoever came through: [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]], [[Redd Kross|d3a4e499-19cf-4676-8aff-4a326b47cdb2]], [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]], the [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]].

years.cap: Brannon with the first line-up, c. 1988
years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: Sonic Youth take them out on the Daydream Nation tour
years.p: The Hyenas record their first album with Vig first, then open dates on [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s American tour.
years.xp:
Strickland, in thrift-store dresses or suits but never jeans, blasting a '72 Stratocaster through a Fender Twin, threw people. Vig called the look and the sound totally at odds. Brannon says club staff kept asking if she was the bass player.

She was also, he says, the one who booked the shows, drew the art, managed the band and drove the van.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
yt: Live at RAPP, New York, July 1989
years.h: You Can't Pray a Lie is Kimball's favorite
years.p: The Stricklands write most of the riffs and Brannon sticks to words. Kimball and Monroe both name Lullaby and Goodnight as their favorite Hyenas song.
years.xp: Trouser Press heard the balance improve here, with Strickland's guitar finally giving Brannon a run for his money. A short European tour with labelmates [[Killdozer|6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38]] followed.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Heroin moves from dabbling to doing
years.p: Metro Times dates it to this period: Brannon and Stolarchuk's addiction becomes hard to miss. Brannon says it cost them opportunities because people were scared of the band.
years.xp: Brannon's own account: it started around the beginning of the band. "Dabbling. Dabbling became doing." He says it was never something they promoted, but it was obvious.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Kurt Cobain gets a tip about Butch Vig
years.p: Backstage at the Ritz with Mudhoney and Sonic Youth, Cobain tells Brannon he likes the sound of the Hyenas' records. Brannon tells him to go see his guy Vig.
years.xp:
Vig confirms the link from his side: Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman passed the Hyenas records to Cobain and Krist Novoselic, and [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] had been listening to them and [[Killdozer|6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38]]. Those records, Vig says, were very influential in his working with Nirvana and the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]].

Brannon also remembers Vig asking, while the Hyenas loaded in at Smart, if he could keep working on a Nirvana mix.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
yt: Everything I Want, live at CBGB, fall 1990
years.h: Life of Crime is the last one with the first line-up
years.p: Cut at Smart in June 1990. Trouser Press called it a dynamo of bad vibes; the band toured hard behind it, including a leg with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] on the Goo tour.
years.xp: A song from the sessions, Save Me Tomorrow, labelled Sexy Rocker on the master tape, stayed unreleased until Third Man's reissue. Brannon's view: by this record they had it down.

eras.title: The rhythm section walks
eras.text: Kimball and Monroe started jamming with P.W. Long of Wig on the side, and the side project became Mule. Brannon and Stolarchuk had split as a couple but kept the band, rebuilding it with ex-Necros.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas · Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Kimball and Monroe leave to make Mule full time
years.p: [[Mule|84189509-850d-428b-a8f0-1626cb0eabb3]], with Long, plays its first show at the Heidelberg in Ann Arbor that spring. By the end of the year Kimball and Monroe are out of the Hyenas.
years.xp: Before the break, Long played guitar on the Hyenas' cover of Alice Cooper's Public Animal #9 for a Sub Pop singles-club tribute, and joined them on it at CBGB at the end of a tour with Wig. Kimball's explanation, years later: the band had run its course, and he and Monroe wanted to try something new.

yt: Let It Burn, live at Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, November 1992
years.h: Brannon calls an old Necros drummer out of the blue
years.p: Todd Swalla, whose mom's basement hosted Negative Approach's first show, joins with Cleveland bassist Kevin Ries. Swalla says it took him about a year to get comfortable with Kimball's parts.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times
years.h: The neighbours think somebody is being murdered
years.p: With Vig too busy after Nirvana, the band cut Crawl with Al Sutton at White Room in Detroit's Capitol Park over a Fourth of July weekend. Brannon's PA blasted out the open third-floor windows.
years.xp:
Sutton told Metro Times a man from the store downstairs came up to see what was happening, watched Brannon screaming into the mic, warned that he'd go hoarse, and left.

Strickland kept one headphone off and her amp so loud she kept asking for more in the cans, until the headphones got hot enough to blister her ear. Sutton says she didn't care.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: Ries quits; another Necro, Ron Sakowski, takes bass
years.p: Swalla says Ries wanted his girlfriend on tour and left over it. Ries died of an overdose shortly after, Metro Times reports.
years.xp: Sakowski got a song list from Brannon, had about two rehearsals and went straight out on the cross-country Crawl tour.

eras.title: Memphis, then nowhere
eras.text: The new line-up toured constantly and nobody could hold a job. The last album slowed down into the blues and gave Brannon room to sing, and the tour behind it ended the band.

years.cap: Laughing Hyenas at Metro, Chicago, January 1993
years.h: The Hyenas open for Fugazi at an amphitheater in Pontiac
years.p: The second line-up plays the Phoenix Plaza Amphitheater in Pontiac, Michigan, ahead of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]]. Fugazi is on the list of bands Metro Times counts as Hyenas fans.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Trouser Press
years.h: Brannon couldn't listen to Hard Times for years
years.p: Recorded in Memphis at Easley McCain in June 1994. Doug Easley plays pedal steel on a Johnny Cash cover, Home of the Blues; Brannon hears the closer, Each Dawn I Die, as the band's goodbye.
years.xp:
Brannon told Metro Times it was a personal album about what he was going through, and that only Third Man's reissue got him listening again. Engineer Davis McCain remembers him nervous at the start and happy by the end, and Strickland knowing exactly what she wanted.

Trouser Press heard it differently: weary sludge rock from a band sounding disengaged.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times
yt: Live at the Engine Room, Fort Worth, March 1995
years.h: Strickland springs Brannon from rehab on day 25: there's a tour
years.p: Brannon had checked into a 30-day program with his mother's help. He says he stayed mostly straight on the road except in New York, San Francisco and LA.
years.xp:
Brannon is candid about the state he was in after a bad breakup: overdoses, family who disowned him, a stretch on the street. He also mentions, as a story long since told, getting sick at the Jabberjaw gig in LA and throwing up on Drew Barrymore.

Asked if Stolarchuk and Swalla were also still using: "Yeah, we all were to the end."

years.src: Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Touch and Go won't front the plane tickets
years.p: A two-month European tour with John Peel sessions was booked. Swalla says Corey Rusk asked each member about drugs, wasn't convinced, and the airfare advance never came.
years.xp: Swalla says that was one reason he quit: the label had no faith in them, and he needed out of that life anyway. [[Don Caballero|b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8]]'s [[Damon Che|8e999c8c-ea9d-4181-8611-60f03a67360b]] filled in briefly and cut one song, Shine, before he bailed too.

years.h: Nobody quits. It just stops
years.p: Strickland goes to Florida to care for her parents and tells Brannon she can't do it anymore. Brannon: there was no big fuck-you, it just couldn't happen.

eras.title: Larissa's band, nobody else's
eras.text: Brannon and Sakowski kept playing together for decades, in Easy Action and in a revived Negative Approach. Third Man brought the records back in 2018, and Brannon has refused every invitation to bring the band back without Strickland.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas · Detroit Metro Times
years.h: Brannon and Sakowski start Easy Action
years.p: With ex-Gravitar guitarist Harold Richardson. When Negative Approach reunites, Brannon plays with Richardson and Sakowski rather than the original members.
years.xp: Brannon was arrested for heroin possession in a sting outside Detroit's Comet Bar in 2000 and went cold turkey in a cell at the 13th Precinct. Police, he says, put him in what they called the David Ruffin cell, since he was a musician. He walked out and played Easy Action's record-release show at the Gold Dollar, and that was the end of the habit.

years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
years.h: Larissa Strickland dies at 46
years.p: She dies in North Port, Florida. Metro Times reported a suspected drug overdose.
years.xp:
Brannon's words to Metro Times at the time: "I lost a true friend, my first love, my partner in crime."

In 2023 Rolling Stone put her at No. 181 on its list of the 250 greatest guitarists of all time.

q: Nobody can play guitar like Larissa.
years.src: Detroit Metro Times · Wikipedia: Laughing Hyenas
yt: Brannon sings Everything I Want with Dinosaur Jr., San Francisco, 2017
years.h: Third Man reissues everything, and Brannon rules out a reunion
years.p: Jack White's label puts the whole catalog back on vinyl with unreleased tracks, remastered by [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s Bob Weston. Even with J Mascis or Kim Gordon offered as a stand-in, Brannon says no.
years.xp:
Brannon called a reunion disrespectful to the band and to her. His closing advice to fans: you got the records, enjoy the records.

The closest thing so far came in San Francisco in 2017, when Brannon and Swalla joined [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] onstage for a surprise Everything I Want.

The reissue party was at Marble Bar in Detroit, a short walk from the Cass Corridor house the band fled in 1984.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jim Kimball
years.h: Jim Kimball dies at 59
years.p: After the Hyenas and [[Mule|84189509-850d-428b-a8f0-1626cb0eabb3]] he drummed in the The Denison/Kimball Trio, [[Foetus|934c6bbc-3fc4-4d4a-9280-f02856da0e12]] and, briefly, [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], and played in Chicago's Ghost Forest until 2025.

sources.title: Detroit Metro Times: An oral history of the Laughing Hyenas
